title: The History of Final Fantasy | From 1987 to Remake and Rebirth | Gaming History
description: The full history of Final Fantasy: the original in 1987, Final Fantasy VII, X, XI, XIV, the Pixel Remaster, the VII Remake trilogy and XVI, plus the 200 million sales milestone.

sections.heading: A fantasy that was supposed to be final
sections.script: Crystals, chocobos, giant swords and music you can hum years later. Final Fantasy is one of the most famous role playing series in the world, and it began as a gamble. In this video we walk through the history of Final Fantasy: from the first game in nineteen eighty seven, through the PlayStation era that made the series a global name, to online worlds, remakes and the newest hits. We will look at the dates, the people behind the games and the sales milestones, including the moment the whole series passed two hundred million units. Whether you started with the pixel art classics or with the modern action games, there is a story here for you, because the series has never stopped changing. Grab a potion and let's begin.

sections.heading: The first Final Fantasy
sections.script: The story starts on December eighteenth, nineteen eighty seven, when Square released Final Fantasy in Japan for the Famicom. It was created by Hironobu Sakaguchi, who directed the game and led the project, with a scenario by Kenji Terada. The music came from Nobuo Uematsu, and the character art from Yoshitaka Amano, a pair who would shape the look and sound of the series for decades. The name is often linked to the idea that this might be the last game of Sakaguchi's career if it failed, although Sakaguchi himself later played that story down. Nintendo brought the game to North America in nineteen ninety, published under the Nintendo label. It was a modest start for what would become a giant, and nobody at the time could have guessed that the name would still be alive almost forty years later.

sections.heading: Final Fantasy VII changes everything
sections.script: Then came the PlayStation. Final Fantasy Seven was released in Japan on January thirty first, nineteen ninety seven, and it arrived in the West later that year. It moved the series into three dimensional worlds and told the story of Cloud Strife, a mercenary who joins a group fighting a powerful company, while the villain Sephiroth casts a shadow over everything. Characters such as Aerith became household names among gamers. For many players this was the first Japanese role playing game they ever touched, and it turned Final Fantasy from a niche favorite into a worldwide brand. Even today it is often named among the most influential games ever made, and fans have asked for it to return again and again, which is exactly what Square Enix finally decided to do.

sections.heading: Final Fantasy X and the PlayStation 2
sections.script: In the PlayStation 2 generation, Final Fantasy Ten arrived in Japan on July nineteenth, two thousand one. It was the first game in the series to feature full voice acting, and it introduced fully three dimensional environments across its world of Spira. Players followed Tidus, a young athlete pulled into a strange land, and Yuna, a summoner on a pilgrimage, in one of the most emotional stories the series has told. It remains a fan favorite, and many players still point to it as the moment the series learned to tell stories with real voices.

sections.heading: Going online and the Square Enix merger
sections.script: The next big step was going online. Final Fantasy Eleven launched in Japan on May sixteenth, two thousand two, as the series' first online role playing game, and it was one of the first big games to let players on the PlayStation 2 and on PC play together. Behind the scenes, the company itself was changing. Square, the maker of Final Fantasy, merged with Enix, the maker of Dragon Quest, and on April first, two thousand three, the new company Square Enix came into being. Two rival role playing giants became one, and since then the same company has looked after both series. Both companies had spent years as rivals, each with its own loyal fans, so the news was a real surprise at the time. The merger set the stage for the next twenty years of games, from huge console adventures to long running online worlds.

sections.heading: A Realm Reborn
sections.script: Final Fantasy Fourteen had one of the most remarkable recoveries in gaming. The first version, released in September two thousand ten, received very negative reviews, and Square Enix chose to rebuild the game. Naoki Yoshida was brought in to lead the relaunch, and Final Fantasy Fourteen: A Realm Reborn was released on August twenty seventh, two thousand thirteen, for PC and PlayStation 3. This time the response was strongly positive. Expansions followed, and the game kept growing. By January two thousand twenty four, Square Enix reported more than thirty million registered players. By October two thousand twenty one, it had already become the most profitable game in the series. It is proof that a second chance can change everything, and fans often point to it as the best comeback story in online gaming.

sections.heading: Pixel Remaster brings the classics back
sections.script: While new games arrived, Square Enix also looked back. The Final Fantasy Pixel Remaster collection brought the first six games to modern platforms with redrawn pixel art and rearranged music. It began on July twenty eighth, twenty twenty one, with the first three games on Steam, iOS and Android, and the rest followed, with the sixth game arriving in February twenty twenty two. Later the whole set reached PlayStation four, Nintendo Switch and Xbox Series consoles. In March twenty twenty five, Square Enix announced that the Pixel Remaster series had passed five million units worldwide. It shows how strongly fans still love those early adventures, and the remasters were built to feel faithful to the originals, and it gives newcomers an easy way to experience the series from the very beginning.

sections.heading: The Final Fantasy VII Remake trilogy
sections.script: The biggest event of the last few years was a reimagining of the most famous game in the series. Final Fantasy Seven Remake was released on April tenth, twenty twenty, for PlayStation 4, and Square Enix said it shipped and sold more than three and a half million copies in just three days. By August of that year, the number had passed five million. The story continues in Final Fantasy Seven Rebirth, which arrived on PlayStation 5 on February twenty ninth, twenty twenty four, and the studio has said it is now focused on the third and final part of the trilogy. The remakes keep the heart of the original, but they build a much larger world around Cloud and his friends.

sections.heading: Final Fantasy XVI and a new generation
sections.script: Final Fantasy Sixteen launched on PlayStation 5 on June twenty second, twenty twenty three. It follows Clive Rosfield through a darker world of Eikons, the giant summoned beings, with fast action combat instead of the classic turn based battles. Square Enix announced that the game had passed three million copies within about a week of launch. It also showed how willing the series is to reinvent itself. Final Fantasy has always changed from one game to the next, with new worlds, new battle systems and new heroes. Some fans love the new direction, others miss the old style, but that constant change has helped the series survive for almost forty years.

sections.heading: Two hundred million and your favorite
sections.script: In March twenty twenty five, Square Enix announced that the Final Fantasy series had passed two hundred million units sold worldwide, a number that includes both physical and digital sales. From a hopeful project in nineteen eighty seven to one of the biggest names in gaming, Final Fantasy has grown with every new generation of players. So now it is your turn. Which Final Fantasy is your favorite, and which one should come back next? Do you prefer the classic turn based games, the online adventures or the action remakes? Tell us in the comments. If you enjoyed this history, like the video and subscribe for more gaming history, and we will see you in the next video.
